the lymphoid tissues of the human fetus, as far as they have been studied here, are in a state of development which is in agreement with the ontogeny of these tissues in other species, including the rat and mouse.

in human fetal lymphoid organs the lymphoid cells develop in situ, from a common progenitor population, in relation to the local micro-environment, and in a sequential manner, with a strict spatial and temporal order.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the ontogenetic development of the human lymphoid system, including the spleen, the thymus and the lymph node is a continuous process from the 12 to the 38th week, and that this process is not a series of discrete events, but a gradual maturation, which is reflected in a continuous change of the immunological properties of the different cell populations.
the human fetus has an active immune system, and that this system is fully functional by the 24th week.
